_why: Fixtures for `node tools/check-clone-imports.mjs --selftest`. They live in JSON, not in the gate's own source, because the gate scans text rather than an AST: a fixture like "import x from './a'" written as a JS string literal is indistinguishable from a real import, and when these cases were inline the gate reported nine unresolved imports against itself. JSON is not in its SOURCE list, so the data is inert. Each case is a defect this gate had or would have had.
cases: new URL to a FILE counts
new URL to a DIRECTORY does not
example inside a line comment is not a dependency

// Vite turns new URL('./x.ts', import.meta.url) into an asset
import a from './real';
example inside a block comment is not a dependency

/* import q from './ghost'; */
import a from './real';
an apostrophe in a comment does not swallow the file

// git cannot carry it
import a from './real';
a // inside a string is not a comment
a specifier in a plain string is not an import
import a from './one'; import b from './two';
the same specifier twice is reported once

import a from './dup';
import b from './dup';
an import statement written inside a double-quoted string is data

const entry = "export * from './tauri';\n";
import a from './real';
an import statement written inside a single-quoted string is data

const e = 'import x from "./ghost"';
import a from './real';
an import statement written inside a template literal is data

const e = `export { y } from './ghost';`;
import a from './real';
a string with an escaped quote is data, and the real import after it still counts

const s = 'can\'t import from \'./ghost\'';
import a from './real';
rust: mod x; declares a file
rust: attributes and visibility before mod
rust: an inline module is not a file
rust: mod in a line comment is not a dependency
rust: mod in a nested block comment is not a dependency

/* outer /* inner */ mod ghost; */
mod real;
rust: mod in a string is data
rust: mod in a raw string is data

let s = r#"mod ghost; "quoted" "#;
mod real;
rust: a lifetime does not open a string

fn f<'a>(x: &'a str) -> &'a str { x }
mod real;
rust: a char literal quote does not open a string

let q = '"'; let a = '\'';
mod real;
rust: an identifier ending in mod is not a declaration

let supermod = 1; fn premod() {}
mod real;
